labels.rationale: The prompt explicitly asks for one diagram evolving through a sequence of steps rather than separate slides. Ordered named states are a direct realization of that model.

labels.intent: Represent an ordered sequence of distinguishable steps and associate each step with its active diagram state.
labels.rationale: The requested sequence needs identifiable states, but section/era labels and a particular stable-id schema are optional organizational choices.

labels.intent: Provide narration for every step that remains useful for both live presenting and independent browsing.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires captions and two viewing modes. Separate one-line titles and paragraph-length captions are one reasonable way to serve those modes.
The prompt does not require on-screen step numbering. Correctly maintained manual numbers or an interface without numbers would also satisfy it.

Strongly typed grouped payloads and a cast-free component boundary are internal API choices. The prompt requires reusable components and working output, without specifying TypeScript or this typing discipline.
The prompt describes elements moving and being relabeled within one evolving diagram. Preserving entity continuity while those changes occur is central to that behavior.

labels.intent: Introduce new entities in a visually coherent transition while maintaining continuity of existing entities.
labels.rationale: Elements appearing is explicit, but waiting until all existing entities settle is a chosen animation sequence. Concurrent or otherwise intelligibly coordinated entrances can satisfy the prompt.

labels.intent: When a later diagram state omits an entity, remove it coherently without leaving stale content visible.
labels.rationale: Rendering the active scene correctly requires honoring removals when they occur. An animated exit is a particular transition treatment that the prompt does not explicitly require.

labels.intent: Preserve visual continuity across successive states of the same evolving diagram.
labels.rationale: A single evolving diagram is required, but shared scene groups and retaining the same component instance are implementation mechanisms. Other state and rendering architectures can preserve the same continuity.

labels.intent: Treat continuing entities as the same entities through a transition rather than presenting them as newly introduced content.
labels.rationale: The prompt implies continuity as elements move and change labels. Layout projection and a specific separation of newcomer fade wrappers are optional mechanisms.

Reusable scene components must render authored diagram compositions correctly while elements evolve. Breaking readable, intentional stacking just to accommodate an implementation pattern would make the generated diagram incorrect.
The prompt asks for reusable scene components, without specifying an unstyled kit. A reusable kit with sensible visual defaults can fully meet the request.

labels.intent: Allow reusable scene components and presentation controls to support suitable visual customization across generated presentations.
labels.rationale: Reuse across topics and layouts calls for adaptable visuals. DOM hooks and exclusively presentation-owned CSS are particular ways to provide that adaptability.
A styling-framework dependency is an architectural choice that the starting prompt does not constrain. Reusable components can be implemented with or without one.

labels.intent: Support diagram compositions with deliberately positioned entities and transitions between their step-specific states.
labels.rationale: Elements moving within evolving diagrams requires expressive positioning. Literal coordinates, raw motion elements, and layout ids are particular authoring mechanisms.
The prompt does not ask for repository attribution. Its presence, destination, default behavior, and corner placement are incidental branding choices.
The exact attribution wording is not implied by the prompt.
The prompt does not require an attribution element or a dedicated hook for styling one. Presentations can be complete without this feature.
The prompt makes no request about header branding. A tasteful optional or default brand would not inherently make the presentation incorrect.
The prompt explicitly says viewers should switch between presenting and browsing the presentation.
Viewers must be able to switch modes, but author control over the initial mode is not requested. A sensible fixed initial mode can satisfy the prompt.

labels.intent: Provide a mode suited to live delivery with clear step narration and a diagram-focused presentation.
labels.rationale: A presenting mode needs a useful delivery experience. Hiding all captions, contents, and previous/next controls while showing exactly a marker and one-line title is one possible layout.

labels.intent: Provide a mode for independent reading in which step narration and usable navigation are available.
labels.rationale: Browsing is explicitly requested. The exact collection of titles, multi-line text, indicators, and a wide-screen table of contents is a reference layout choice.
Switching the view mode should preserve the viewer's place in the requested step sequence. An unexpected reset would undermine the basic runtime switching behavior.

labels.intent: Provide conventional keyboard access to forward and backward step navigation.
labels.rationale: A browser presentation should support ordinary keyboard use, particularly during live delivery. The full set of Space and paging aliases is not fixed by the prompt.
Responsive viewing and step navigation can be served by accessible touch controls without horizontal gestures. The prompt does not require swiping.
The prompt requires movement through steps, which previous/next navigation can provide. Direct jumps through a progress indicator are an additional convenience.
Section organization, a table of contents, and jumping specifically to section starts are not implied by the requested browsing mode.

labels.intent: Make the current position understandable to viewers and expose current-state semantics for any applicable navigation controls.
labels.rationale: Usable browsing requires understandable navigation state. Progress indicators, table-of-contents entries, and CSS hooks are particular ways to expose it.
Normal interactive controls must retain their keyboard behavior in a browser presentation. Moving the scene as an unintended side effect of operating a focused control is a correctness defect.

labels.intent: Handle navigation at the first and last steps predictably without entering an invalid or blank presentation state.
labels.rationale: Robust step navigation needs defined endpoint behavior. Clamping is reasonable, but a clearly communicated loop or completion behavior could also meet the prompt.

labels.intent: Keep the diagram readable, compositionally coherent, and capable of clean entity transitions across screen sizes.
labels.rationale: The prompt explicitly requires the presentation to look right at different sizes. A uniformly scaled fixed canvas is one solution; responsive layouts can also work.
The prompt gives no canvas dimensions. Other dimensions or a responsive canvas can satisfy it.

labels.intent: Fit the scene appropriately within the available space in both presenting and browsing modes.
labels.rationale: Responsive layout must work in both requested modes. Separate fit-geometry definitions are a specific implementation technique.
The prompt does not prescribe an interview format. Batched questions or generating from the supplied topic can be reasonable skill workflows.

labels.intent: Develop a coherent narrative and visual plan from the topic, with content and diagram states for the presentation steps.
labels.rationale: Turning a topic into a presentation requires deciding the story and its visuals. Obtaining the style and every step description through user gathering is one way to make those decisions.

The prompt asks for a skill that turns a topic into a presentation, allowing it to supply sensible style and step details. Requiring questions for every omitted detail is an additional interaction policy.

A skill that turns a topic into a presentation must be able to generate missing details rather than require the user to specify every step. Letting the user build with partial detail is central to that request.
Proceeding directly from a complete prompt is sensible, but the starting prompt does not prescribe whether additional useful questions may be asked.
ASCII mockups and confirming layouts before building are optional authoring aids. Neither is needed for a complete topic-to-presentation skill.
The prompt explicitly requires the skill to work in a project without the reusable components already set up. Detecting and supplying missing prerequisites in an appropriate location is necessary.

labels.intent: Provide a working application build setup capable of producing the generated browser presentation.
labels.rationale: Building generated presentations is required. Vite, React, TypeScript, and the exact npm command are specific stack choices.

labels.intent: Provide reusable, topic-independent scene infrastructure for step states, evolving entities, captions, navigation, viewing modes, and responsive rendering.
labels.rationale: These core behaviors follow directly from the prompt. A particular stage contract, table of contents, and fit-scaled canvas are implementation choices within that infrastructure.
An explicit presentation registry with a route for each entry is not necessary to generate browser presentations. Standalone outputs can meet the prompt without a shared presentation index.
A skill intended to work in existing projects must recognize compatible infrastructure by its behavior. Replacing it merely because formatting or names differ would be an avoidable robustness defect.

labels.intent: Ensure all runtime, build, and verification dependencies required by the chosen implementation are available when bootstrapping.
labels.rationale: Working without existing setup requires a complete dependency installation. The reference's particular framework, motion, icon, linting, and browser libraries are not prescribed.
The prompt does not require an unstyled or framework-neutral scaffold. A functioning scaffold with reusable default styling would also satisfy it.

labels.intent: Locate required bootstrap and authoring resources reliably regardless of the invocation working directory.
labels.rationale: The skill must work in projects that have not been set up, which requires reliable access to its resources. Resolving everything relative to SKILL.md is one mechanism.

labels.intent: In an unprepared project, supply everything needed to build, run, and verify a generated presentation before declaring it ready.
labels.rationale: Bootstrapping from missing infrastructure is explicit. The three-anchor structure and presentation index are choices within a complete setup.
When compatible infrastructure already exists, the skill should use it. Re-scaffolding a functioning project unnecessarily risks disrupting the setup the prompt expects the skill to build on.
Supporting projects with missing setup requires filling gaps while preserving working infrastructure. Replacing already usable parts would be an avoidable integration defect.

labels.intent: Integrate presentation infrastructure into a monorepo in an appropriate application location without disrupting the repository's existing workspace structure.
labels.rationale: Working in existing projects implies respecting their structure. A self-contained presentations/ app is one suitable location, rather than a required directory name.
Scaffolding at the root is a location choice. A standalone presentation app in a suitable subdirectory can be equally complete in an empty or standalone repository.

labels.intent: Choose a safe scaffold target in an existing project and resolve material target ambiguity before making disruptive changes.
labels.rationale: Bootstrapping must protect existing project contents. Mandatory confirmation for every non-empty project is one policy; clear prior authorization and an unambiguous safe target can also suffice.

labels.intent: Produce an accessible browser presentation as a coherent output that can coexist with existing project content.
labels.rationale: The generated result must be usable and must preserve existing work. A dedicated folder, route, and shared registry are particular packaging mechanisms.

labels.intent: Keep presentation-specific visual choices configurable without making reusable scene infrastructure depend on one presentation's design.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires reusable scene components. Presentation-owned CSS, host themes, component parameters, or other separation mechanisms can maintain that reuse.
The starting prompt does not choose a styling method. Plain CSS and framework-based styling can both produce the required browser presentation.
Generating a presentation in an existing project must not destroy other presentations or make them inaccessible. Preserving existing work is an obvious robustness requirement.

The prompt explicitly requests generation from a topic, without asking for a dedicated editing capability. Modifying existing presentations is useful but its absence need not make generation incomplete.

labels.intent: If a request involves editing existing presentation content, identify the intended target before applying changes.
labels.rationale: Protecting existing work is required for a project-integrating skill. Listing all presentations and asking a particular question is only one way to resolve an ambiguous target.
A specialized modification dialogue that avoids the creation flow is not requested. Other effective editing procedures, or a skill focused on generation, can satisfy the starting prompt.
The prompt requires the skill to check that generated output builds and renders, and requires the presentation to look right. Verifying those properties before claiming completion is necessary.

labels.intent: Inspect enough rendered steps and viewport sizes to establish visual coherence and catch significant layout and responsive defects.
labels.rationale: Visual and responsive correctness is required. The exact first/last/dense-step sampling rule is one reasonable inspection strategy.
Checking the generated build and render must affect whether the skill reports success. Known failures must be fixed and the result rechecked before completion.

labels.intent: Run browser inspection using reliably available tooling and dependencies, and obtain settled views with relevant diagnostics accessible for review.
labels.rationale: Reliable build and render checking is explicit. Preferring a particular local helper and placing temporary scripts under the project root are tooling arrangements rather than required outcomes.

labels.intent: Ensure generated presentation code builds successfully without compilation or applicable type-checking errors.
labels.rationale: Clean builds are directly requested. npm run build and a typed implementation are particular choices for realizing them.
A generated browser presentation must open and render its initial state without runtime or console errors. The prompt explicitly calls for checking rendering.
The prompt explicitly assigns a caption to each step and asks viewers to move through steps. Forward and backward navigation is a basic realization of that movement.
Every generated presentation must use the explicitly requested evolving-diagram model. Generating independent slides would contradict the core request.

labels.intent: Ensure important diagram content and presentation controls remain readable, fit the available display area, and avoid accidental obstructive collisions.
labels.rationale: Looking right across screen sizes includes basic composition correctness. A fixed canvas and particular chrome components are optional ways to arrange it.

labels.intent: Review evidence of possible visual defects, correct actual readability and navigation-state problems, and distinguish intentional composition from accidental collisions.
labels.rationale: The requested visual correctness makes actual defects relevant. A helper warning workflow and explicit overlap markers are one way to review and resolve them.

labels.intent: Make displayed controls legible and distinguish the current navigation state, keeping presentation-specific visual choices adaptable for reuse.
labels.rationale: The requested browser interaction needs usable controls. Attribution, presentation-owned CSS, and a kit with no visual defaults are optional parts of the reference solution.

labels.intent: Verify the complete generated application build and fail on errors in any included presentation or required application infrastructure.
labels.rationale: Checking that generated output builds requires a complete relevant application build. A shared index and a specific npm script are implementation choices.

labels.intent: Include a working sample in the repository that users can access as a reference presentation.
labels.rationale: The prompt asks for a sample presentation made using the skill. Committing it and registering it through a particular application registry are packaging choices.
The prompt explicitly says to use the skill to make the sample. Building the sample by an unrelated process would fail that instruction.

labels.intent: Make the sample teach how to use the presentation skill through the kind of presentation the skill produces.
labels.rationale: The sample's instructional topic and production by the skill are explicit. Its exact title and closing self-reference reveal are narrative choices.

labels.intent: Make the instructional sample demonstrate the same evolving-diagram presentation model required of generated presentations.
labels.rationale: The sample must be a presentation of the requested kind. A top conversation row, accumulating tray, reveal frame, and never-moving entities are particular compositions.
The prompt does not prescribe a step count, section count, era names, or canonical outline. A different instructional sequence can explain the skill fully.
The exact opening title, caption, and you/prompt visual are sample content choices. Another opening can explain the skill's topic input.
The prompt does not require an interviewing workflow or this particular explanatory beat. Its exact wording, nodes, arrow, and question chip are incidental sample choices.
A complete sample can explain the presentation model without depicting gathered answers as cards in a tray. This precise beat, wording, and placement of morph information are not required.
Growing a stationary card tray is a sample storytelling choice. The prompt permits other sequences and compositions, including moving existing entities.
The sample is not required to devote a step to specifying depth. The exact caption, ghost card, and partial/full control are optional ways to explain author input.

The product must use reusable scene components, but the instructional sample need not depict that internals detail through a particular beat. A scene-kit socket, tray treatment, title, and caption are sample choices.

The skill must check builds and rendering, but the sample need not teach that behavior in a dedicated pipeline beat. The exact verification node, green check, title, and caption are optional explanatory content.
A modification loop is not explicitly requested for the skill or sample. The edited card, modify arc, title, and caption are optional narrative choices.
Using the skill to produce the sample is required, but announcing that fact in a closing reveal is optional. Another ending can explain how to use the skill.

labels.intent: Automatically confirm that the required instructional sample is present, usable, and has the intended step content in the intended order.
labels.rationale: Verifying the generated sample supports the explicit sample and automation requests. Matching nine reference steps and their verbatim titles and captions is unnecessary.
The requested sample is a required deliverable. A check intended to verify that sample cannot correctly pass when it is absent.

labels.intent: Exercise every sample step and its navigation in a rendering environment faithful to the browser presentation, detecting runtime and console errors.
labels.rationale: The requested automatic verification should cover the step sequence rather than only an initial successful render. A production preview and a particular browser execution arrangement are mechanisms.

labels.intent: Use a consistently reachable preview endpoint for server startup, readiness checks, and browser navigation across supported environments.
labels.rationale: Reliable automated rendering requires the browser to reach the preview server. IPv4 loopback is one solution; another consistently configured host can also work.
Runtime errors or failed transitions contradict the required rendering and navigation behavior. Automatic verification must fail and give enough step context to diagnose the problem.
A way to verify presentations automatically needs a clear machine-detectable outcome and actionable failure reporting. Non-zero failure status is the ordinary command-line realization.
An automatic verifier must clean up servers it owns even after failure. Leaked processes would make repeated checking unreliable and interfere with the user's environment.

labels.intent: Provide repeatable access to rendered step layouts for checking visual correctness, with inspection results available to the author.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires correct appearance and rendering checks. A separate project-local per-step screenshot helper, production preview, desktop size, and artifact directory are particular inspection arrangements.

labels.intent: When capturing or assessing a step's final rendered appearance, wait until its transition has completed.
labels.rationale: Meaningful visual checks must assess the intended settled layout. A configured fixed settle interval is one way to establish readiness.
Visual correctness is required, but an automatic overlap-warning detector with element-level diagnostics is optional. Browser inspection or other layout checks can establish correctness without it.
The prompt does not require an overlap detector or subtree exemption markers. Intentional readable overlap can be supported and reviewed through other mechanisms.
Readable active navigation matters, but automatically warning about visual similarity is an optional diagnostic feature. Other verification can catch an unusable active state.
Attribution is not requested, so warnings about its presence, size, appearance, or styling hook are not required.
The prompt does not prescribe whether visual artifacts inform manual review or automated pass/fail checks. Either can be appropriate when it reliably establishes correctness.
Adding an agent skill that creates browser-based presentations from a topic is the prompt's direct request.

labels.intent: Supply reusable scene-building resources that the skill uses to generate presentations across topics and projects.
labels.rationale: Reusable scene components are explicit. React, templates, and scripts are a particular mix of resources for satisfying that requirement.
The prompt explicitly asks for build/render checking, a generated sample, and a way to verify presentations automatically. A verification flow covering that output is required.
Export formats are not requested, but a harmless optional export feature would not inherently make the browser presentation incomplete or incorrect. The prompt does not explicitly prohibit exports.

A general-purpose visual editor would add a substantial separate product and authoring workflow beyond the requested agent skill. Treating that expansion as required scope would reasonably draw objection.
A production hosting or publishing workflow adds operational scope beyond generating and verifying browser presentations. The prompt gives no request for that expansion.
The prompt requires successful builds, rendering, and automatic verification. Subjective taste scores as the primary verification mechanism would not establish those objective requirements.

labels.intent: Provide an agent procedure that uses reusable scene infrastructure and includes checks for generated output quality.
labels.rationale: The prompt asks for both a skill and reusable components, so supporting infrastructure must accompany the procedure. The exact hybrid packaging of templates and scripts can vary.

labels.intent: Provide a documented, repeatable automation interface that checks the relevant application build and presentation step rendering.
labels.rationale: Automatic verification is explicit. One npm run verify entry point is convenient, but other commands or a small orchestrated set of checks can satisfy it.

labels.intent: Verify rendered presentation behavior in an environment that accurately exercises browser layout, transitions, and runtime failures.
labels.rationale: Actual browser presentation rendering needs a faithful check. Playwright, Chromium, and vite preview are one tooling combination rather than mandated technologies.

labels.intent: Let verification enumerate the presentation steps and determine which step is active reliably.
labels.rationale: Automatic checks of the evolving sequence need observable progress. Dedicated count/index data attributes are one option; semantic UI state or another supported interface can work.
A root landing page, slug routes, and an unknown-path fallback describe an optional multi-presentation application shell. Standalone browser presentations can satisfy the prompt.
The prompt does not require a shared registry, manual entries, or lazy loaders. Auto-discovery or independently accessible presentation outputs can be reasonable.
A pathname switch with no routing dependency is an implementation choice. The starting prompt does not constrain routing libraries.

labels.intent: Provide reusable, topic-independent building blocks for expressing diagram entities and their evolving relationships.
labels.rationale: The prompt directly asks for reusable scene components. The exact box/label/arrow/frame/emphasis/symbol-chip set and parameter interface can vary.
The prompt does not require icons, Lucide, or an icon-as-component API. Other glyph techniques or presentations without icons can satisfy it.

labels.intent: Ensure bootstrapped projects receive compatible, working reusable scene infrastructure as the skill and its components evolve.
labels.rationale: Working in projects without setup requires a dependable distribution of the scene components. A snapshot in templates, its canonical source location, and parity tests are one maintenance mechanism.
Runtime mode switching is required, but the exact P shortcut is not implied. A mode control or another accessible interaction can provide switching.
The prompt specifies both modes without selecting an initial mode for the sample. Opening in either mode can be correct.
